releasesInRange.name: pnpm 12.9
releasesInRange.body:
This release runs pnpm in StackBlitz WebContainers, adds a per-registry `networkConcurrency` setting, and records every installed project in the store. It also carries a security fix for `pnpm login`.

### Minor Changes

- pnpm now automatically uses WebAssembly in StackBlitz WebContainers, including when installation scripts are disabled. Native installations continue to use the native executable when installation scripts are enabled.

- A `registries` entry can now set `networkConcurrency`, the most requests pnpm keeps in flight to that registry's origin. Requests to other registries keep the overall limit. The setting may live in `pnpm-workspace.yaml` or the global `config.yaml`.

  ```yaml
  registries:
    https://npm.corp.example.com/:
      scopes: ["@acme"]
      networkConcurrency: 4
  ```

- `pnpm install` now records every project it installs in the store's `projects` directory, as a symlink to the project directory. A `--frozen-store` install without the global virtual store still records nothing. Only projects that used the global virtual store were recorded before [#6929](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/6929).

### Patch Changes

- `pnpm login` no longer forwards credentials in its request body to another origin during redirects.

#### Installing packages

- Fixed `pnpm install` failing on Android with `ERR_PNPM_STORE_DIR_ACQUIRE_OPERATION_LOCK` [#16508](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16508).

- `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` again succeeds when a workspace project recorded in `pnpm-lock.yaml` has no directory, such as a project left out of a Docker build context. It still fails if the project's directory exists without a `package.json` [#16453](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16453).

- `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` no longer requires a `pnpm-lock.yaml` in a project that has no dependencies. It also succeeds when `pnpm-lock.yaml` records only the pinned pnpm version, as other commands write it when they run before the first install [#16477](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16477).

- Fixed `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` rejecting a fresh lockfile when an injected workspace dependency has an optional peer supplied by another workspace project [#16428](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16428).

- With `nodeLinker: hoisted`, a filtered install now keeps the packages of the workspace projects an earlier install put in `node_modules`. This also covers the install that `pnpm --filter <selector> run` and `pnpm --filter <selector> exec` start before the command. Before, these installs removed every package that only the unselected projects needed [#16483](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16483).

- `pnpm install` with `nodeLinker: hoisted` now refreshes directories supplied by custom fetchers when reinstalling. pnpm also keeps the symlinks inside those directories.

- With `enableGlobalVirtualStore` on, scripts can run entry points that a CommonJS require hook loads again, such as `ts-node index.ts`. They failed
…(truncated)

releasesInRange.name: pnpm 12.9.1
releasesInRange.body: This release moves the WebContainer build into a separate `@pnpm/wasm` package, shrinks the `pnpm` package back to about 4 MB, and fixes `pnpm publish` with provenance from GitLab CI. ### Patch Changes - The WebAssembly build for StackBlitz WebContainers now ships as a separate `@pnpm/wasm` package. The `pnpm` and `@pnpm/exe` packages no longer include it, which brings their unpacked size back from about 55 MB to about 4 MB. In a WebContainer, install `@pnpm/wasm` with npm to get the `pnpm` command. - `pnpm publish` with provenance from GitLab CI is no longer rejected by the npm registry with a 422 error. The provenance statement now includes the GitLab CI variables in `invocation.parameters`, as npm does [#16551](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16551). - `pnpm audit signatures` now uses the TLS settings of the redirect target when a registry redirects its signing-keys request, for example to registry.npmjs.org. A `cafile` scoped to a private registry no longer makes the redirected request fail [#16541](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16541). - Fixed `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` rejecting an up-to-date lockfile when an injected workspace package uses a catalog entry in `peerDependencies` [#16557](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16557). - The `[]` filter selector works again with Git 2.24 through 2.27 [#16561](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16561). With Git older than 2.24, the selector now fails with an error that names the required Git version. It also detects changes in projects whose directory names contain non-ASCII characters. Such a change used to be credited to the parent project. `changedFilesIgnorePattern` and `testPattern` now match changed files whose names contain non-ASCII characters. - The `pnpm` executable is about 10% smaller. On macOS arm64 it went from 45.1 MB to 40.3 MB. - Sped up trust downgrade checks for packages with long release histories. - With `optimisticRepeatInstall: false`, `pnpm install` now runs the projects' own lifecycle scripts, such as `prepare`, even when `node_modules` is already up to date [#16545](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16545). - `pnpm self-update` now fails for Homebrew-installed pnpm and prints the `brew upgrade` command for the installed formula, such as `brew upgrade pnpm` or `brew upgrade pnpm@11`. It used to install a second copy of pnpm that the Homebrew one kept shadowing [#16547](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16547). ## Platinum Sponsors

releasesInRange.name: pnpm 11.28.4
releasesInRange.body:
pnpm 11.28.4 fixes two ways credentials could leak, makes `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` accept several lockfiles it rejected, warns when an optional dependency cannot be fetched, and stops `pnpm self-update` from installing a second pnpm next to a Homebrew one.

### Patch Changes

* `pnpm login` no longer forwards credentials in its request body to another origin during redirects.

* The error for a tarball that fails its integrity check no longer prints credentials, query strings, or fragments from the tarball URL.

#### Installing packages

* `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` now succeeds in a project with no dependencies when `pnpm-lock.yaml` records only the pinned pnpm version. Other commands write such a lockfile when they run before the first install. A lockfile missing the `---` line after that section is accepted too [#16477](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16477).

* `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` again succeeds when a workspace project recorded in `pnpm-lock.yaml` has no directory, such as a project left out of a Docker build context. It still fails if the project's directory exists without a `package.json` [#16453](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16453).

* `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` no longer fails with `ERR_PNPM_OUTDATED_LOCKFILE` for a workspace project that declares `dependenciesMeta` and whose dependencies are all workspace links. pnpm now records that project's `dependenciesMeta` in `pnpm-lock.yaml` [#16457](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16457).

* Fixed frozen installs replacing a hoisted dependency with a workspace package of the same name. A later `pnpm dedupe` then removed the hoisted link [#16485](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16485).

* With `enableGlobalVirtualStore` on, scripts can run entry points that a CommonJS require hook loads again, such as `ts-node index.ts`. They failed with `ERR_UNKNOWN_FILE_EXTENSION` on Node.js versions without built-in TypeScript support [#16436](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16436).

#### Optional dependencies

* `pnpm install` now prints a warning with the error when an optional dependency cannot be fetched and is skipped. The skipped package is no longer linked into `node_modules` as a broken symlink or listed among the added dependencies. The `pnpm:skipped-optional-dependency` log reports the skip with the `fetch_failure` reason [#16514](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16514).

* When an optional dependency fails to build, pnpm now removes its link from `node_modules`. A repeat `pnpm install` then reports "Already up to date" and no longer reruns the failing build [#16468](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16468).

* Fixed frozen installs creating symlinks to the working directory for skipped optional dependencies and unresolved peer dependencies [#16454](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16454).

#### Hoisted node_modules

* With `nodeLinker: hoisted`, a filtered install now keeps the packages of the workspace projects an earlier install put i

prs.title: refactor(resolver): drop the installable flag the walk never reads
prs.author: KSXGitHub
prs.body:
## Summary

Removes `DependenciesTreeNode::installable`, the `installable: bool` parameter of its constructor, and the four copies the peer walk made of it on the way to `DependenciesGraphNode::installable`. Nothing read any of them. Behavior is unchanged.

**What the flag was**

- The port of the TypeScript resolver's `installable`: whether an optional dependency fits the host (`os`, `cpu`, `libc`, `engines`) and may be skipped. In v11 a `false` stops the fetch and the link.
- In pacquet every one of the 18 construction sites passed `true`, and the field's own doc said so.
- pacquet makes that decision elsewhere: the deps-restorer's installability pass checks every lockfile snapshot against the host at install time and builds the skipped set. The resolver had nothing to record.

**Evidence that it was dead**

- Deleting only the tree node's field: the compiler reports one reader, the walker's copy into `NodeEntry`, and one writer, the constructor.
- Deleting only the graph node's field: the compiler reports its two writers in `finalize.rs` and no reader. With the whole chain removed, every crate and test target in the workspace type-checks; the only other sites were 20 test fixtures setting `installable: true`.
- Mutation: storing the inverse of the passed value in the constructor, so every node carried `false`, left the resolver's 429 tests and the 23 CLI smoke tests of the affected selection green.

**What changed**

- `DependenciesTreeNode::new(resolved_package_id, childr

prs.title: feat: support pnpm in StackBlitz WebContainers
prs.author: zkochan
prs.body:
## Summary

Make the regular pnpm v12 npm package run in StackBlitz WebContainers. It includes the shared Rust CLI compiled to WebAssembly and a Node host for filesystem, network, process and terminal operations. The package selects WASM automatically from the WebContainer runtime marker, including when installation scripts are disabled. Native installations with scripts enabled replace all four launchers with the native executable and retain direct native execution.

Related to pnpm/tasks#63. The core workflows and distribution selection are covered here; the task also tracks the remaining command-by-command portability audit.

The regular npm wrappers bundle the complete WASM payload and its locked, patched dependencies. Release builds prepare this payload without restoring CI compilation caches. Native executable archives remain native-only. The separate `pnpm-wasm.tgz` remains available for testing. Both distributions are exercised in Chromium WebContainers.

Browser verification found and fixed a WASI path-normalization defect affecting paths with multiple parent segments, including workspace package packing. It also showed that WebContainer's npm skips local-tarball installation scripts. Node launchers now work without those scripts, while verified npm and pnpm installation/rebuild flows restore direct native execution outside WebContainers.

prs.title: fix: take file locks with flock on Android
prs.author: lazerg
prs.body:
## Summary

Closes pnpm/pnpm#16508.

Since 12.6.0, every install takes a shared store operation lock through `File::lock_shared`. On Rust 1.97, which this repo pins, std returns `Unsupported` for `File::lock`, `File::lock_shared`, and `File::try_lock` on Android, so `pnpm install` on Termux fails with `ERR_PNPM_STORE_DIR_ACQUIRE_OPERATION_LOCK`. Android does have `flock`, and std calls it from Rust 1.98 on.

The store lock is not the only std file lock on that path: `pnpm install` also takes the metadata transaction lock (`install-coordinator`) with `File::lock`, which fails the same way once the store lock succeeds. `main` already had `pnpm_fs::lock_file` and `pnpm_fs::try_lock_file` for the WASI build, with a cfg pair at each call site. They now exist on every target: `libc::flock` on Android, std elsewhere, host leases on WASI. Every file lock goes through them: the store operation lock, the metadata transaction lock, `DirLock`'s held file, private installs, concurrency-group slots, and the pipeline agent lock.

I bumped the toolchain to 1.98.1 first, but clippy then fails on new lints in unrelated crates, so the fallback stays in `pnpm_fs` until the toolchain moves.

How I checked: I ran `cross test --target aarch64-linux-android -p pnpm-store-dir --lib store_lock` with the NDK r25b image from `Cross.toml`. On `main`, the four tests that take the lock fail with the error from the issue (`lock_shared() not supported`). With the store-lock change, all 8 pass. `pnpm-fs` pass
…(truncated)

prs.title: fix: warn when an optional dependency cannot be fetched
prs.author: zkochan
prs.body:
## Summary

An optional dependency whose tarball cannot be fetched (a 404, an integrity mismatch) was skipped with no warning. Both CLIs are affected:

- pnpm v12 counted the package in `Packages: +N` and emitted no `pnpm:skipped-optional-dependency` event.
- pnpm v11 behaved the same, and also left a dangling `node_modules/<name>` symlink and listed the package under "optionalDependencies: + …".

This PR adds a `fetch_failure` reason to `pnpm:skipped-optional-dependency`, with the error code and message in `details`. Both default reporters render it as a warning:

```
[WARN] is-number@7.0.0 is an optional dependency that could not be fetched. Excluding it from installation.
ERR_PNPM_TARBALL_INTEGRITY: Failed to verify the integrity of https://registry.npmjs.org/is-number/-/is-number-7.0.0.tgz: Integrity check failed.
```

v12 also stops counting the skipped package in `pnpm:stats added`. v11 removes failed packages from the graph and from the direct dependencies, so they are no longer linked, hoisted, or built.

A parent package links its children while downloads are still running, so both CLIs also left a dangling link to a failed optional child inside the parent's `node_modules`. Both now remove those links once the fetch results are known.

The warning shows up whichever workspace project the install runs from: the skip carries the lockfile directory as its prefix, so both reporters render a `fetch_failure` skip without the usual current-project filter.

The v11 integrity

fix(update): bound the Workspace column of the interactive prompt
prs.author: lazerg
prs.body:
## Summary

Closes pnpm/pnpm#16518.

In a recursive `pnpm update --interactive`, a dependency shared by many workspace projects joins all their names into one `Workspace` cell. Nothing bounded that cell, and `column_widths` pads every row of the group to the widest cell, so a 12-project workspace made each row 454 columns wide and the prompt's selection drawing stopped matching the screen. pnpm 11 builds the same long line (its table gives the Workspace column no width), but its prompt redraws the soft-wrapped rows correctly, so the symptom is v12-only.

Wrapping doesn't fit here, since the checkbox prompt draws one line per choice. So the cell is bounded at 30 columns, the width `outdated -r` wraps its `Dependents` column at. Past that it names as many projects as fit and counts the rest (`example-workspace-package-01, +11 more`). The first project is always named in full, so a long first name can take the cell a little past 30.

## Squash Commit Body

```text
The Workspace cell of the interactive update prompt joined every project
a dependency was found in, with no bound. Since column_widths pads every
row of a group to its widest cell, one dependency shared across a large
workspace pushed all rows of its group far past the terminal, and the
prompt's redraw no longer matched what the terminal showed.

Cap the cell at 30 columns, the width outdated -r wraps its Dependents
column at. Past it, name the projects that fit and count the rest

prs.title: fix(resolver): leave out an optional dependency whose subtree cannot be resolved
prs.author: zkochan
prs.body:
## Summary

Closes pnpm/pnpm#16511.

pnpm 12 failed with `ERR_PNPM_FETCH_404` (or `ERR_PNPM_NO_VERSIONS`) when a regular dependency of an optional package could not be resolved. The reported case is `sharp` 0.35. Its optional `@img/sharp-freebsd-wasm32` and `@img/sharp-webcontainers-wasm32` depend on `@img/sharp-wasm32`, which the reporter's mirror does not serve.

This PR applies npm's rule, which gives the same result on every platform. When a dependency fails to resolve anywhere below an optional dependency, pnpm leaves out the nearest optional dependency above it, together with its subtree. If a package needs that subtree through regular dependencies only, the install still fails with the original error.

pnpm 11 avoids the failure differently. It resolves the subtree of an optional package as optional only when that package does not fit the current platform, so the lockfile it writes depends on the machine it runs on. A Linux run locks `sharp-freebsd-wasm32` without `sharp-wasm32`, and a FreeBSD frozen install of that lockfile is then incomplete. pnpm 12 does not copy that rule.

How it works:

- **Walk** (`walk/failed_edge.rs`): a failed regular edge inside an optional subtree no longer aborts. Its parent is recorded as broken in the workspace context. The existing guard still applies: if the wanted lockfile holds a satisfying entry, the failure stays fatal.
- **Prune** (`resolve_workspace/broken_optional.rs`): it runs on the merged tree before peer resolution. A packag
…(truncated)

pnpm.io release pages are now generated from the release instead of being written by hand. One page is written per stable v11 and v12 release, patches included.

- DOCUMENTATION.md, RELEASING.md and the release-notes skill describe the new page.

fix(resolver): revalidate uncacheable registry metadata instead of refetching it
prs.author: zkochan
prs.body:
## Summary

Since 12.8.0 (pnpm/pnpm#15722), pnpm records a metadata mirror as uncacheable when the response's `Cache-Control` has `max-age=0`, `no-cache`, or `no-store`. The next install then requested that packument with no `If-None-Match` or `If-Modified-Since`, so it downloaded and parsed the whole document again on every install.

bit.cloud proxies npm packuments with `cache-control: public, max-age=900, no-store`, so a Bit workspace re-downloads every packument on every install. That is the regression in the issue. It shows up through the Node-API addon only because that is how Bit installs. The same CLI install against registry.npmjs.org (`public, max-age=300`) never sets the flag, which is why the CLI comparison found no difference.

This PR keeps the validators for an uncacheable mirror and adds `Cache-Control: no-cache` to the request. An intermediary must then revalidate with the origin, and the origin answers a current mirror with a 304. The fix is in both stacks, since pnpm/pnpm#15722 changed both.

Closes pnpm/pnpm#16528

Bit 2.2.73 on macOS arm64. Each run is `bit install next webpack jest typescript eslint rxjs @angular/core vue` in a fresh `bit init` workspace with a warm store and cache, using `PNPM_NAPI_BINARY` to pick the addon. Max RSS comes from `/usr/bin/time -l`.

| published 12.7.0 | 226-232 MB | 4.0-5.1 s |
| published 12.8.0 / 12.8.2 | 443-495 MB | 15-19 s |

prs.title: fix(lockfile): accept injected catalog peers in frozen installs
prs.author: altaywtf
prs.body:
## Summary

`pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` now accepts an up-to-date lockfile when an injected workspace package declares a catalog peer dependency.

Closes pnpm/pnpm#16557.

All four new CLI cases fail on unfixed main. The no-catalog unit regression fails without its guard. The final four CLI regressions also passed after the last edit. All push hooks passed, including TypeScript compile/lint, Rust formatting, Clippy, rustdoc, Dylint, typos, and Taplo. The full test suite and Windows/Linux reproductions were not run locally.

prs.title: fix(store.path): fall back to the home store when the project directory is not writable
prs.author: lazerg
prs.body:
## Summary

Closes pnpm/pnpm#16554.

To pick the default store, pnpm 11 creates a temp file in the project directory and checks whether it can be hard linked into the pnpm home directory. When the current directory is not writable, creating that file throws, so `pnpm store path`, `pnpm store status` and other commands that resolve the store fail with `EACCES`, `EPERM` or `EROFS`. Now these permission errors fall back to the store in the home directory, the same result as when the probe finds no linkable place. pnpm 12 already does this: its link probe treats a failed file creation as "not linkable" and ends up on the home store, so this is a v11-only fix.

## Squash Commit Body

```text
The default store lookup creates a temp file in the project directory to
test whether it can be hard linked into the pnpm home directory. When the
directory is not writable, creating the file throws EACCES, EPERM or
EROFS, and every command that resolves the store fails, including pnpm
store path and pnpm store status.

Treat a permission error while creating the probe file as "nothing to
link" and use the store in the home directory, which is also what pnpm
12 resolves to in this case.

Closes pnpm/pnpm#16554
```

## Checklist

- [x] I checked the referenced issue and verified that none of the PRs
  already linked to it solves it.
- [x] New features are implemented only in the Rust pnpm v12 CLI. Bug fixes
  are implemented in every affected version.
- [x] Added a changeset (`pnpm changeset`) 
…(truncated)

prs.title: fix(publish): include invocation parameters in GitLab provenance
prs.author: lazerg
prs.body:
## Summary

Closes pnpm/pnpm#16551.

`pnpm publish` with provenance from GitLab CI fails with a 422 from the npm registry. The registry checks `invocation.parameters.CI_PROJECT_URL`, `CI_COMMIT_SHA`, `CI_PROJECT_ID` and a few more in the SLSA v0.2 predicate against the signing certificate, and `gitlab_statement()` never wrote `invocation.parameters`. The GitHub Actions statement uses SLSA v1 and is not affected.

The GitLab statement now carries `invocation.parameters` with the same variable list as npm's `libnpmpublish`. Variables that are not set are left out, as npm does. pnpm 11 publishes through `libnpmpublish`, so this only affects v12. I could not run a real GitLab publish, so the check is a unit test on the generated statement.

## Squash Commit Body

```text
The npm registry verifies a GitLab CI provenance statement by comparing
invocation.parameters (CI_PROJECT_URL, CI_COMMIT_SHA, CI_PROJECT_ID,
CI_PROJECT_NAMESPACE_ID, CI_PIPELINE_SOURCE, ...) with the claims of the
Fulcio certificate. The statement had no invocation.parameters, so every
publish with provenance from GitLab CI failed with 422.

Add the block with the GitLab CI variable list npm's libnpmpublish uses.
Unset variables are left out, as they are in npm's JSON.

Closes pnpm/pnpm#16551
```

## Checklist

- [x] I checked the referenced issue and verified that none of the PRs
  already linked to it solves it.
- [x] New features are implemented only in the Rust pnpm v12 CLI. Bug fixes
  are implemented in eve

prs.title: fix(pnpr): allow Quay's CDN hosts for OCI layer redirects
prs.author: lazerg
prs.body:
## Summary

Closes pnpm/pnpm#16548.

Quay answers blob requests with a 302 to `cdn01.quay.io` (and its other `cdnNN` hosts). `oci_download_allowed` only knew the CDN hosts of Docker Hub and GHCR, so pnpr refused the redirect and returned a 502 for every layer pulled through a `https://quay.io/` upstream. This adds `cdn.quay.io` and `cdn01` to `cdn06.quay.io`, the hosts Red Hat lists for Quay pulls, to the allowlist for the `https://quay.io` origin. Credentials still stay on the registry origin.

I pulled `fedora/fedora-minimal` blob `sha256:d8695176...` through a local pnpr with the config from the issue: 502 before the change, 200 with a matching digest after.

## Squash Commit Body

```text

Closes pnpm/pnpm#16561.

Since 12.7 and 11.28, the `[<since>]` selector runs `git diff --no-relative ...`. git added `--no-relative` in 2.28. Older git, for example 2.25 on Ubuntu 20.04, prints the `git diff` usage text and exits with 129, so filtering fails with `ERR_PNPM_FILTER_CHANGED`.

## Summary

Closes pnpm/pnpm#16573

cmd.exe reads a batch file one line at a time, by byte offset, and reopens the file for every line. The `pnpm.cmd` that pnpm 12.8 and older linked ran `pnpm.exe` as a command of the batch, so cmd.exe was still reading it while `pnpm.exe` ran. (`pnpm self-update` links the new shim from the running pnpm, and the batch-ending shim from pnpm/pnpm#16509 shipped in 12.9.0, so the glitch needs such a `pnpm.cmd` on disk and a running 12.9.0 or 12.9.1: in the report, a 12.8.x self-update had written the shim, and 12.9.0 replaced it.) When `pnpm self-update` replaced the file (the write is already an atomic rename, which makes no difference since cmd.exe reopens by path) and exited, cmd.exe read on in the new, longer shim from the offset where the old target line ended. It ran the tail of line 4 (`INE=!CMDCMDLINE:/c=!"`), printed that it is not recognized, and ran the new shim's last line, which started `pnpm self-update` once more.

When the linker writes a `.cmd` shim that ends its batch before its target (the pnpm CLI's), it reads the `.cmd` it replaces. If that one keeps its batch, the new shim is laid out so that the byte offset where cmd.exe reads on in the old file is the start

On Windows that line names the shell's status, not the script's: `cmd` ends with `STATUS_CONTROL_C_EXIT`, shown as `exit code -1073741510`, and PowerShell (the reporter's `script-shell`) ends with `exit code 1`.
